title: 往北三块石板  (Three Stones North)

segments.t: Saturday dawn breaks softly over Courtyard Inn in Chengdu. While the upstairs guests are still asleep, Qing, Chen, and Zhou tiptoe out to the quiet courtyard carrying a brass lantern and a flat iron bar. Listen first.
你们俩小声点——现在才星期六早上六点半！
帮我轻轻把一号桌抬到一边，别让桌腿刮响。
小晴，趁我还没碰石板，把明信片上的线索再念一遍。
那位退休制图员写道：从院子的老树往北数三块平石板。
在我自己的院子里哪边是北呀？我的眼镜去哪儿了？
周经理，您的眼镜就在眉毛上面呢，北边对着大门。
第一块、第二块，这儿就是边缘灰浆松了的第三块石板。
老陈，用你的木头把手敲敲中间——听起来真是空的吗？
听下面清脆的回声：这块石板底下有个小空间。
自从三十年前下大雨的那个五月，就没人抬起过这块石板！
老陈，千万小心啊，换一块院子石板可贵了！
退后半步，我把扁铁棒伸到角落下面。
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
你们俩小声点——现在才星期六早上六点半！

'Whisper, both of you—it is only half past six on Saturday morning!' "Xiaosheng" joins "small" and "voice" for speaking in a low whisper, while "cai" before the time stresses how early half past six feels.
帮我轻轻把一号桌抬到一边，别让桌腿刮响。
'Help me lift table number one aside gently so the legs do not scrape.' Doubling "qing" into "qingqing" paints a careful, light touch, and "zhuo tui" pairs "table" with "leg" just like English.
小晴，趁我还没碰石板，把明信片上的线索再念一遍。
'Read the postcard clue one more time before I touch the stones, Qing.' "Mingxinpian" literally means "open-letter slice"—a postcard whose message travels without an envelope.
那位退休制图员写道：从院子的老树往北数三块平石板。

'The retired mapmaker wrote: Count three flat stones north from the old shade tree.' Directions in Mandarin use "wang" ("toward") plus the compass point, so "wang bei" guides your eyes straight north.
在我自己的院子里哪边是北呀？我的眼镜去哪儿了？
'Which way is north in my own courtyard? Where did my glasses go?' Asking "nabian"—"which side"—is the natural way to ask "which way", and "yanjing" pairs "eye" with "mirror" for glasses.
周经理，您的眼镜就在眉毛上面呢，北边对着大门。
'Your glasses are sitting above your eyebrows, Zhou, and north faces the front gate.' "Meimao" combines "brow" and "hair" for eyebrows, while "damen"—literally "big door"—is the main courtyard gate.
第一块、第二块，这儿就是边缘灰浆松了的第三块石板。
'Stone one, stone two, and here is stone three with the loose mortar edge.' Adding "di" before a number turns "one, two, three" into "first, second, third", and "shiban" joins "stone" with "slab".
老陈，用你的木头把手敲敲中间——听起来真是空的吗？
'Tap the middle with your wooden handle, Chen—does it really sound hollow?' Repeating "qiao" as "qiaoqiao" gives the friendly sense of "give it a quick tap", and "kong" means "empty" or "hollow".
听下面清脆的回声：这块石板底下有个小空间。
'Listen to that clear echo underneath: there is a small space below this stone.' "Huisheng" literally means "returning sound"—an echo—while "dixia" points to the space right underneath.
自从三十年前下大雨的那个五月，就没人抬起过这块石板！
'Nobody has lifted this flagstone since that rainy May thirty summers ago!' Notice how "sanshi nian qian" puts "before" at the very end of "thirty years" to say "thirty years ago".
老陈，千万小心啊，换一块院子石板可贵了！

'Please be careful, Chen, because replacement courtyard stones cost a small fortune!' "Xiaoxin" literally urges someone to keep a "small heart"—to take great care—while "ke gui le" stresses how pricey new stone slabs are.
退后半步，我把扁铁棒伸到角落下面。
'Stand back half a step while I slide the flat bar under the corner.' "Tuihou" joins "retreat" and "back" for "step back", and "ban bu" neatly says "half a step".
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.
你们俩小声点——现在才星期六早上六点半！
帮我轻轻把一号桌抬到一边，别让桌腿刮响。
小晴，趁我还没碰石板，把明信片上的线索再念一遍。
那位退休制图员写道：从院子的老树往北数三块平石板。
在我自己的院子里哪边是北呀？我的眼镜去哪儿了？

第一块、第二块，这儿就是边缘灰浆松了的第三块石板。
老陈，用你的木头把手敲敲中间——听起来真是空的吗？
听下面清脆的回声：这块石板底下有个小空间。
自从三十年前下大雨的那个五月，就没人抬起过这块石板！
老陈，千万小心啊，换一块院子石板可贵了！
退后半步，我把扁铁棒伸到角落下面。
Three flat stones north of the old tree, the hollow flagstone is ready to rise after thirty quiet years. See you in the next scene.
回头见！
